## What this is

<!-- TODO(author): rewrite in your own voice. Draft below is a placeholder so the page renders. -->

A timeline of the AI tools I've actually leaned on for coding — not every chatbot I poked at, just the ones that stuck in my daily workflow. It starts in November 2021 with VS Code Copilot, goes quiet for a few years, then picks up again in late 2024 when AI-assisted coding became core to how I work.

Entries are **adoption dates, not exclusive use**. Claude Code (CLI / agentic) and Antigravity (IDE) coexist today — one didn't replace the other. Where a tool *did* replace another in the same slot (Antigravity → Cursor as IDE), I'll say so.

## What didn't stick

Not everything I tried made the timeline. These are tools I gave a real go and then dropped — sometimes because something already in my workflow was doing the job better, sometimes because the switching cost outweighed what they offered, and occasionally because I never got past first-contact friction.

::: {.didnt-stick-list}

::: {.didnt-stick-card}
**GitHub Copilot agentic features**

— tried them when they landed; they weren't as good as what I already had — ChatGPT for assisted coding, then Cursor and Claude Code for agentic work. No reason to switch.
:::

::: {.didnt-stick-card}
**Gemini CLI / Codex**

— at the time I tried these, Claude Code was already doing the same job better. Neither showed me a reason to switch.
:::

::: {.didnt-stick-card}
**Mistral Vibe**

— tried it on launch day and got stuck linking my chat account. Might be that it expects an API key even when a chat account is linked; haven't gone back to confirm.
:::

::: {.didnt-stick-card}
**Zed**

— fast and clean, but I lean too hard on VS Code's search and the rest of its ecosystem to move my main editor.
:::

:::

## On my radar

A mix of new things I haven't tried yet and old things I dropped but keep watching — tools change, and so do my needs.

- **Zed** — they keep shipping impressive updates, so I take another look every few months.
- **Mistral Vibe** — the docs and integration may have moved past launch-day jank; worth another real try.
- **Codex CLI** — I'm on the Codex app when I want Codex; curious what the CLI does differently.

## How I add to this

An entry lands on the timeline once a tool has earned **sustained daily use** — not a weekend trial, not a "this is cool" demo. If I went back to the previous tool within a couple of weeks, it doesn't make the timeline. The point isn't to log every tool I touched; it's to mark the moments my actual workflow changed.

A tool lands in **What didn't stick** under a parallel bar: I gave it a real trial and made a conscious decision to drop it. Things I saw a demo of and moved on from don't count — that's bookmarking, not trying.
